extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for the Academy of Management (AOM) Annual Meeting (Division & Interest Group reviewers; Teaching & Learning Conference reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing reviews of papers and symposia submitted to the Academy of Management Annual Meeting, covering tone, format, section-specific evaluation criteria, and symposium-specific considerations. Applies to empirical, conceptual, and symposium submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on AI tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools is not permitted in the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit rule: reviewers must not use AI-based tools when preparing reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer constructive, respectful, and developmental feedback; even when identifying unresolvable issues, provide suggestions for improving the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong reviews also highlight the manuscript's strengths and offer specific, actionable guidance. Remember each review represents both your DIG and the Academy; maintain professionalism and respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on intellectual contribution and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should focus on intellectual rigor, potential contribution, and the ability to stimulate scholarly dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be open to diverse theoretical frameworks and methodological approaches given AOM's interdisciplinary membership; assess whether submission can stimulate discussion and advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit by deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your review by the deadline; the Annual Meeting schedule does not allow extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is mandatory—late reviews cannot be accommodated due to schedule constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear structure and formatting of feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure your feedback clearly—numbered comments are recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to specific pages, tables, or figures where appropriate; a strong review is typically one single-spaced page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve review anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include identifying information or attempt to uncover authors’ identities. Double-blind (papers) and single-blind (symposia) processes must be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid any actions or wording that could reveal or attempt to discover author identities; respect the applicable blind-review protocol for the submission type.

rubrics_metrics.name: General: Theoretical development
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the submission's theoretical development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the topic is situated within management and organizational scholarship and whether it meaningfully extends existing theoretical conversations (see Introduction criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: General: Methodological rigor (if empirical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the methodological rigor of empirical submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate design, sampling, data collection, validity, and analytical transparency (see Method section for detailed items).

rubrics_metrics.name: General: Conceptual clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess clarity of concepts, arguments, and the logical flow of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for well-defined concepts, consistent application, and clear articulation of the line of argument (especially for conceptual papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: General: Contribution to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the submission’s contribution to the scholarly literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the paper offers novel insights that extend existing literature and whether it stimulates discussion or debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: General: Practical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the practical relevance of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider meaningful implications for both scholarly and practice communities, and whether the 'so what?' threshold is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'So what?' threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should meet the 'so what?' threshold and offer meaningful implications for scholarly and practice communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work lacks clear implications or significance, note this and suggest ways to strengthen relevance and implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symposium: audience quality expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the session likely to meet audience expectations for quality?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the symposium's design, topics, and presenters match what attendees expect from the DIG and AOM Annual Meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symposium: broad appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the symposium appeal to a broad segment of the DIG and AOM membership?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the session engages multiple members and is not excessively narrow in focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symposium: innovation, relevance, and value
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the symposium offer innovation, relevance, and clear value?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the session provides novel perspectives, practical or scholarly relevance, and a clear contribution to attendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction section criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the topic relevant to management and organizational scholarship? Is the research question clearly stated and well-motivated? Does it extend an existing theoretical conversation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a well-motivated problem statement, clear research question, and explicit linkage to and extension of relevant theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: General readability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the submission coherent and well-organized? Do all sections align conceptually and structurally? Are there areas where development suggestions would help?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify places where structural or editorial changes would improve clarity; comment on flow, organization, and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory section criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the theoretical framework clearly articulated and logically constructed? Are concepts well defined and consistently applied? Do hypotheses or propositions follow logically from the theory? Is the literature review robust and appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and internal logic of theory, definition and consistent use of key constructs, appropriateness and comprehensiveness of literature cited, and logical derivation of hypotheses/propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method (Empirical Papers) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Are design, sampling, and data collection clearly explained and justified? Is there internal and external validity? Are analytical methods appropriate and transparent?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether methods are described sufficiently to judge validity and replicability; note potential biases, sampling limitations, measurement issues, and appropriateness of analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings (Empirical Papers) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Are results clearly presented and plausibly interpreted? Are theoretical insights advanced? Are limitations addressed and alternative explanations considered?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check clarity of tables/figures, appropriateness of interpretation vis-à-vis the data, whether results tie back to theory, and whether authors acknowledge limitations and competing explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line of argument (Conceptual Papers) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the reasoning clear, precise, and persuasive? Is the conceptual contribution novel and well-positioned?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess logical coherence of arguments, strength of conceptual claims, novelty relative to existing work, and positioning within the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings (Conceptual Papers) criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Are conceptual insights original, transferable, and clearly articulated? Is the scope of contribution discussed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clearly stated conceptual advances, discussion of generalizability/transferability, and transparent scope/limits of contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution section criteria (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission stimulate discussion or debate? Are implications for theory, practice, and society thoughtfully developed? Are novel insights offered that extend existing literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether implications are substantive and actionable, whether societal/practical consequences are considered where appropriate, and whether the work meaningfully extends the literature.
